newsitem.title: USA: Krantor Corp says injunction lifted.
newsitem.headline: Krantor Corp says injunction lifted.

text.p: Krantor Corp said Tuesday that its motion to dismiss an injunction against the company that barred it from selling inventory has been upheld in federal court.
The ruling frees the company to sell off its kosher frozen poultry and dairy products, exit the kosher business and concentrate on selling frozen squid, a company spokeswoman said.
It expects to finalize charges in the third quarter related to the discontinuation of the kosher line and expects to be profitable in the fourth quarter, the company said.
The size of the charge has not yet been determined, a spokeswoman said.
Krantor said that all injunctions placed against it and Affiliated Island Grocers by Empire Kosher Poultry have been lifted by further court order.
But Krantor said it is continuing to pursue its counter-claims against Empire, alleging destruction of property and business in connection with its discontinued kosher food business.
Krantor contends that Empire's business conduct has caused significant losses to its operations in the first two quarters of 1996.

The company also contends that Empire's legal actions "unnecessarily blocked Krantor from pursuing its profitable promotional wholesale business while the injunction was in effect and therefore limited its business activity in the third quarter."
Krantor said it believes that the losses incurred as a result of Empire's alleged actions were in excess of $5 million since the inception of the kosher business in 1995.
